meta.title: Privacy · Beamlynx
meta.description: What Beamlynx collects, why, and what you can turn off. Your databases, queries and data never leave your computer.

heading: Privacy
intro: Beamlynx is made by Grephyte ApS, a Danish company (CVR 37931535). This page says what we collect, why, and what you can turn off. Questions go to <email/>.

sections.title: Your databases stay on your computer
paragraphs: The Beamlynx app runs on your computer. Your queries, your connections and their passwords, and the data you see never leave it. We can't see them.

sections.title: Usage stats in the app
paragraphs: Each time the desktop app opens, it sends one event. If you are signed in, the event is tied to your account. If not, it is tied to a random ID made on your computer, not to you.

The app also sends detailed usage stats: when you add a connection (only the database type, such as PostgreSQL), and how many queries ran each hour (only whether you or an AI agent ran them, and whether they were Pine or SQL). You can turn these off at any time in Settings → Account → Send detailed usage stats. The event when the app opens is sent either way.
Every event also carries the app version, operating system and processor type. PostHog receives the events and records your country from your IP address.
The app tells you about this the first time it starts, before anything is sent.

sections.title: Signing in
paragraphs: Each time the app starts, it asks whether you want to sign in with GitHub or Google, until you do. It's optional, and the app works the same either way.

If you sign in, we store your email address, the name on that account, which of the two you used, when you first and last used Beamlynx, and your app version and operating system. Your usage stats, including each time the app opens, are then linked to you. We use this to know who uses Beamlynx.

sections.title: This website
paragraphs: beamlynx.com counts page views and clicks with PostHog. If you sign up for the newsletter, Substack stores your email address and sends the newsletter, and your visits here are linked to that address in PostHog. If you sign in to the app with detailed usage stats on, the browser you sign in with ends on a page here, and its visits here are linked to your account.

sections.title: Who handles it
paragraphs: PostHog stores the usage stats and website visits, and Supabase stores sign-ins. Both store them in the EU. GitHub and Google handle the sign-in itself, under their own privacy policies. Substack handles the newsletter. We don't sell your data or share it with anyone else.

sections.title: Why we're allowed to
paragraphs: We count usage and visits because we have a legitimate interest in knowing how Beamlynx is used, and by whom. You can turn the detailed usage stats off. To object to the rest, email <email/>. We store your sign-in because you chose to sign in.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Email <email/> to see what we have about you, or to have it deleted. Signing out of the app stops linking new usage to you, but doesn't delete what is stored.
We keep the data until you ask us to delete it, or until Beamlynx is shut down. You can also complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet).
